candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, pesticides table row (Aldrin)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Row supplies MQL, effluent concentration (Ce), derived instream acute concentration (2.13*Ce), and multiple candidate criteria values; different readings of which column is operative or how 1E+100 placeholders apply would change the enforceable limit chosen for Aldrin.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, pesticides table row (Alpha-BHC)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Blank Ce and Ca versus explicit zeros in criteria columns affects whether a limit is deemed established, whether instream screening applies, and whether missing effluent data is treated as no applicable numeric limit or as a documented zero-concentration basis.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, pesticides table row (Diazinon)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Missing MQL and blank Ca/Ce fields alongside nonzero criteria values affect whether Diazinon has an enforceable limit, whether monitoring/reporting thresholds are defined, and how absent reported results are classified.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, pesticides table row (Chlordane)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specified Ce and multiple numeric criteria provide competing limit candidates; interpretation of which criterion is most stringent and whether TMDL N/A removes a limit changes the applicable enforceable concentration.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the receiving stream is not designated for the particular uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines when no enforceable numeric limit exists versus when a limit must still be computed, and whether missing measurements should be treated as outside compliance comparison scope.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the potential instream w aste concentrations are less than the chronic w ater quality criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Gates limit establishment on instream screening results; different interpretation of instream concentration calculation or chronic-criteria column selection changes whether a numeric effluent limit is imposed.

candidates.exact_span: The most applicable stringent criteria are used to establish effluent limitations for a given parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Controls limit-selection logic when multiple criteria columns apply to the same pollutant; alternative readings of 'most applicable' or 'stringent' yield different enforceable limits.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality criteria apply at the end-of-pipe for acute aquatic life criteria and discharges to public lakes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Changes the point of compliance and which acute criteria are directly enforceable at effluent versus instream, affecting the numeric limit used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If background concentration exceeds the w ater quality criteria, w ater quality criteria apply. And "Need TMDL" show n to the next column of Avg. Mass
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links ambient/background concentration and TMDL designation to whether criteria-based limits apply and how Need TMDL N/A entries interact with limit establishment and unresolved cases.
Defines the monthly average effluent limit derived from the daily maximum; a different divisor or applicability rule changes the enforceable monthly comparison value.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, Applicable water quality-based limits formula
candidates.exact_span: Daily Max. Conc. = Cs + (Cs - Ca)(F*Qa/Qe)                            Monthly Avg. Conc. = Daily Max. Conc. / 1.5
candidates.computation_change_reason: Core calculation for translating water quality standards into effluent concentration limits; different variable assignments or formula application change computed daily and monthly enforceable limits.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, Applicable water quality-based limits formula definitions
candidates.exact_span: Cs = Applicable w ater quality standard
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies which table criterion value becomes Cs in the limit equation; ambiguity in selecting the applicable standard changes the calculated effluent limit.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, Applicable water quality-based limits formula definitions
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ambient concentration feeds the limit formula and background-exceedance logic; blank versus reported Ca values in the table affect both computed limits and classification of missing ambient evidence.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, Applicable water quality-based limits formula definitions
candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (1.0 is assigned to domestic w ater supply and human health uses)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mixing fraction assignment by use category changes the dilution allowance in the limit equation and therefore the enforceable effluent concentration.

candidates.locator: page 37, section fact_sheet, Applicable water quality-based limits formula definitions
candidates.exact_span: Qa = Criteria Low flow (4Q3) or Harmonic Mean flow for Human Health Criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Flow term selection (4Q3 versus harmonic mean) alters Qa in the limit formula and can change the numeric effluent limit for human-health versus other criteria.

candidates.exact_span:

                   AND ESTABLISH EFFLUENT LIMITATIONS FOR ALL APPLICABLE PARAMETERS
